newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end higher on soybean rally.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end higher on soybean rally.

text.p: CBOT soy product futures ended higher Tuesday after a late rally in the soybean pit pushed prices higher on the close, traders said.
Modest comission house buying also contributed to the sharp jump in soyoil prices. ADM Investor Services and Prudential Securities were both noted buyers, pit sources siad.
Soymeal prices received support from market talk that both Italy and Egypt were looking for soymeal for import, but the business could not be confirmed.
Cold weather in the U.S. Plains, Midwest and in Europe continued to support soymeal, traders said.
Livestock eat more in cold weather and transportation problems are expected to cause pent-up demand from end users, traders said.

However, weakening soymeal basis levels could pressure futures in the near term, some sources noted. Cash soymeal basis offers continued to weaken, and some offers have fallen as much as $5.00 per ton since Monday.
Soymeal ended up $0.50 to $1.00 per ton, with January up 1.00 at $229.70. Soyoil was up 0.15 to 0.25 cent per lb, with January up 0.20 at 23.15 cents.
On the day, Cargill bought 200 lots March soymeal and Continental Grain bought 150 March, 300 May and 100 July.
Refco sold 250 lots March soyoil. Cargill bought 200 lots March soyoil and Cargill Investor Services bought 400 March.

Soyoil futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 20,000 contracts, below the 28,861 traded Monday. Soymeal futures volume was estimated at 17,000 contracts, below 25,781 traded Monday, the exchange said.
